subject: Kite-6B intermittent 5xx/timeouts — customer notice and recovery updates
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme-retail.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme SRE <sre-acme@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 504s/timeouts from kite-6b in prod

Hi Naomi,

We're seeing a spike in 504/5xx errors for requests routed to kite-6b between 08:45 and 09:05 PDT this morning. It's impacting recommender API responses — about 7% of requests are failing with a 504 or "generation timed out" message. No config changes on our side.

I attached a small request/response snippet and trace from one of the failures (kite6b-request-snippet.txt). Can Redwood confirm whether there were any infra or model incidents on your side?

Thanks — would appreciate a quick acknowledgement and ETA for an update.

--
Liam O'Neill
SRE, Acme Retail
liam.oneill@acme-retail.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme-retail.com>, Acme SRE <sre-acme@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 504s/timeouts from kite-6b in prod

Thanks for the report, Liam — acknowledged, we're on it.

Ben/Diego/Marissa — can you triage? Initial telemetry (internal: trace id 0x5e8b) shows a sudden tail-latency spike and repeated 5xx responses from hosts running kite-6b quantized kernel v2.2. Observed symptoms:
- 504s correlated with long prompt lengths (~1.2k tokens) + high concurrency.
- Error signature: "KV cache miss -> kernel fallback -> execution timeout" in logs.

Immediate asks:
1) Ben: confirm whether autoscaling triggered for the pool; check scale-up latency metrics.
2) Diego: pull the kernel-level traces and heap profile for the time window (08:30–09:10).
3) Marissa: prepare an external-facing acknowledgement to the customer with ETA; start planned traffic steering to kite-3b as a temporary fallback if safe.

I'm attaching the snippet Liam sent and a quick trace we captured (kite6b-trace-20270816.log).

I'll coordinate mitigation and keep Liam updated.

- Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Incident Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 504s/timeouts from kite-6b in prod

Quick update — triage notes below and mitigation applied: 

What we saw:
- Autoscaler did not scale fast enough; metric threshold was based on 1m CPU util which lagged the latency spike.
- Hosts running quantized kernel v2.2 hit a code path that caused repeated kernel fallback and increased per-token time.
- Result was queue growth + 504s at the load balancer.

Actions taken (10:00–10:02):
- Enabled aggressive circuit breaker for kite-6b (fail-open to kite-3b) on Acme's route. Traffic steering started at 10:01 PDT.
- Killed and replaced 3 problematic hosts; rolling restart of the kite-6b pool initiated.
- Collected heapdumps from two hosts (heapdump-20270815.tgz).

Impact: ~85% of traffic for Acme is now served by kite-3b fallback; error rate dropped from ~7% to ~0.6% for affected routes. Latency for fallback model increased median by ~30ms but is within Acme's SLO.

Next steps:
- Diego to analyze heapdump for root cause and escalate to runtime team if kernel bug reproducible.
- We'll prepare a short customer message summarizing RCA and ETA for full kite-6b restoration.

Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme-retail.com>, Acme SRE <sre-acme@acme-retail.com>

Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: kite-6b: incident resolved — summary and next steps

Hi Liam / Acme SRE team,

Thank you for flagging this morning's spike — this is a summary and next steps now that we've restored normal service.

What happened (summary):
- Between ~08:42–09:05 PDT we observed an elevated 5xx/504 rate on hosts serving kite-6b for Acme routes.
- Root cause (short): an unsafe kernel fallback path in the quantized kernel v2.2 triggered by long prompt lengths and high concurrency. That path caused repeated micro stalls that led to queueing and timeouts. Autoscaler thresholds delayed scale-up, amplifying the impact.

What we did:
- At ~10:01 PDT we throttled traffic to kite-6b for Acme and enabled automatic fallback to kite-3b (temporary measure).
- Replaced affected hosts and collected diagnostics (heapdump-20270815.tgz, kite6b-trace-20270816.log).
- Reverted the problematic quantized kernel change for the kite-6b pool and applied a safe rollback to kernel v2.1.
- Deployed a hotfix that prevents the kernel fallback loop in the specific code path; rollout completed by 15:30 PDT and verified.

Customer impact:
- Error rate for Acme routes peaked at ~7% and dropped to <1% after fallback. Median latency increased modestly on fallback but stayed within agreed SLOs. No data loss occurred.

Follow-ups & next steps:
- We will post a detailed postmortem with timelines and technical RCA to the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/kite6b-postmortem-draft (draft available; final copy by 2027-08-20).
- We'll adjust autoscaler thresholds for the kite fleets and add a latency-based autoscaler signal to reduce scale-up lag.
- We'll run a regression test for quantized kernel v2.2 against long-prompt scenarios prior to any future rollouts.

Attachments: kite6b-request-snippet.txt, kite6b-trace-20270816.log, heapdump-20270815.tgz

Apologies for the disruption — we'll reach out once the postmortem is finalized and with any recommended config changes for Acme to avoid similar exposures.

If you'd like a quick sync call to walk through the RCA, I'm available tomorrow morning.

Best,

Naomi Feldman
Incident Manager, Redwood Inference
